risks: accept() docstring | high | Claims that digest verification prevents laundry attack; relies on drift_mod.digest_ok which is not in chunk. | Confirm digest_ok implementation in drift module.
accept() docstring | medium | Claims that refresh() needs no check because it rescans; not verifiable here. | Check refresh() in drift module.
main() | low | Uses analyse_once, build, load_narrative, write_map, refresh, inventory_mod.refresh; none defined in chunk. | Ensure all imported functions exist and are correct.

handoff.purpose: Implement accept() function and main() CLI entry point for architecture mapping tool.

symbols.name: accept
symbols.note: Accepts a drift item by recording it in the snapshot. Performs schema and digest checks before re-signing.

symbols.name: _render_text_summary
symbols.note: Internal helper to format summary text from data dict.

symbols.name: main
symbols.note: CLI entry point; dispatches to accept, check, or default map generation and re-baselining.

claims.text: THE INHERITED BYTES ARE VERIFIED BEFORE THEY ARE RE-SIGNED. Inheriting and then calling ``write_snapshot`` re-signs whatever it was handed, so this verb was a laundry: hand-edit ``islands`` (``--check`` says INVALID SNAPSHOT), then run ``--accept`` on any unrelated item, and the hand-edited lists come back out under a freshly computed, perfectly valid digest with the real finding erased -- three shipped commands, no Python, exit 0. A snapshot whose digest does not verify is not something to build on, so this refuses and writes nothing.
claims.why: The code at lines 1442-1446 calls drift_mod.digest_ok(snapshot) and returns False if it fails, refusing to write. The docstring claim is implemented here.

claims.text: :func:`~daedalus.mapping.drift.refresh` needs no such check because it rescans the tree instead of inheriting.
claims.why: The refresh function is not defined in this chunk; its behavior cannot be verified.

claims.text: Carried over from the snapshot VERBATIM, including the ignore configuration it was taken under and every mechanical list, so recording a reason cannot bank unrelated drift. write_snapshot re-signs the digest, which is legitimate ONLY because the digest it is replacing was verified above -- otherwise this is the laundry described in the docstring.
claims.why: The code builds state dict from snapshot.get() calls and then calls drift_mod.write_snapshot(snap_path, state, acceptances). The digest verification at lines 1442-1446 ensures the snapshot is valid before carrying forward.

claims.text: Gate mode writes nothing, so unlike drift.check it cannot create the baseline it is missing -- and a gate reporting OK against nothing is the exact failure this subsystem exists to prevent.
claims.why: In the --check branch, the code prints the gate text and returns 1 if data["gate"]["first_run"] is true, without writing any file.

claims.text: The SAME analysis the page was rendered from. Re-scanning here would bank a tree that is a few seconds older than the one just published.
claims.why: The code passes reports (from analyse_once) to both write_map and drift_mod.refresh, ensuring the same analysis is used for both.

claims.text: The feature census, from the SAME reports, for the same reason: it used to be typed by hand and it was thirty commits stale while the picker read it as the top of the work queue. Generating it here is what makes 'it cannot be older than the run that produced it' true rather than intended.
claims.why: The code calls inventory_mod.refresh with the same reports variable, ensuring consistency.

observations.what: accept() function performs schema version check and digest verification before carrying forward snapshot data and re-signing.
main() function has multiple branches (--accept, --json, --check, default) and calls several external functions not defined in this chunk.
The docstring of accept() contains a detailed security claim about preventing a 'laundry' attack via digest verification; this is implemented in the code.
The --accept branch returns early after calling accept() and printing result, never reaching the re-baseline code.
In the default branch, the code prints gate text and then calls refresh and inventory_mod.refresh with the same reports, ensuring consistency.
